synoptic.summary: A ridge holds through Friday with a deep, strengthening valley inversion and hazy air: light, terrain-driven wind on Thursday. Flow from ~150°–195° increases Friday ahead of a trough, but the inversion may keep the stronger wind aloft off the surface. The trough swings through Saturday (80% chance) with widespread valley rain from early morning, flow turning to ~300°–330° by Saturday afternoon and the coldest air of the season Saturday night. No thunderstorm risk is mentioned; the hourly forecast shows only 4–10% thunder on Friday evening and Saturday.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Southerly flow will start to increase on Friday ahead of our weekend storm. Winds will be elevated across western Utah, but these strong winds might not manifest near the surface across the Wasatch Front which would limit mixing and allow inversions to hold on until precipitation and cooler air aloft arrive on Saturday.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport (KSLC) sea-level pressure 1025.0 mb at 01:54Z, down from 1027.4 mb 23 h earlier (low point 1024.3 mb at 22:54Z). High pressure still dominates; the slow fall is the first sign of the weekend trough.

observations.summary: Wednesday evening (18:15–18:30 local) observations, ~13 h before the Thursday morning slot. Light wind everywhere (0–6 kt). The Lehi station already shows the evening drainage at 131°–143° 4–10 kt; Salt Lake airport is still at 250°–280° 4–5 kt and South Valley Regional at 290° 4 kt, matching the airport forecast's switch to 150° after 03Z. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data. Valley readings: add 3–8 kt for launch height.

warnings.title: Flow below 160° — rotor off the hills toward ~135°
warnings.why: With flow from 140°–155° the hills toward ~135° from launch put the launch area in their lee; rotor can be present even when the sock looks light.
warnings.triggered_by: Winds aloft 141°–157° at 6–15 kt (1,900–3,700 ft above landing), launch forecast 150°–160° (GFS, NWS hourly forecast)
warnings.investigate: Watch the sock and streamers: launch only when the wind is steady from 160° or more. If it sits at 140°–155° or cycles, wait or walk away.

warnings.title: Wind increase before launch
warnings.investigate: A clear increase on launch before you go → do not launch.

d2-am.explanation: Classic ridge morning: inversion, light drainage at 6–7 kt (gusts to 11) and no mixing threat. The catch is direction: the launch forecast sits right at 160°, and the flow above launch is 141°–157°, which is the rotor direction for this site. Observations from Wednesday evening (Lehi 131°–143°) agree. If the sock shows a steady 160°–195°, it's a good morning; if it stays below 160°, don't launch.
